title: Empty exFAT writes enlarge EOF and may allocate clusters

also_seen_in.verdict: static source follow-up for the exFAT direct empty-write path at bc12195df. No runtime verdict

mechanism: ExfatInode::write_at (and write_direct_at) has no write_len == 0 guard, so offset + 0 > file_size takes the extension path: clusters are allocated, the page cache grows, and inner.size is set to the offset while the call returns 0. The zero-length errno probe in do_sys_pwritev reaches the same path.
contract: write(2): a zero-count write to a regular file returns 0 without causing any other effect.
observed: pwrite64(fd, buf, 0, 4096) on a 2-byte exFAT file returned 0 and set st_size to 4096. Empty pwritev at 8192 and lseek+write(0) at 16384 also enlarged the file and raised st_blocks.

repro.how_to_run: Build test_bugMC-7_exfat_empty_pwrite.c statically as /init, attach fresh ext2 (/dev/vda) and exFAT (/dev/vdb) images, boot. MC7_RESULT REPRODUCED means the bug fired. empty_write-regression.patch is an unexecuted regression test for the fix batch.
repro.runtime_status: REPRODUCED at 604948581 for buffered I/O (01b MC-7, SMP=2, Level 0). Regression test NOT_RUN

caveats: Historical reproduction covers buffered I/O only. The direct path is a static observation. The 01b confirmation claimed O_DIRECT alignment rejects len == 0, but the pin source (is_block_aligned treats 0 as aligned) and the 2026-09-16 audit disagree. Fix batch is uncommitted and runtime-unvalidated by user request.
